title: LINK: Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-Node Propagation Rule Learning for Traffic Kriging
abstract: arXiv:2611.20521v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Spatio-temporal traffic kriging aims to reconstruct traffic time series at unobserved locations with no historical traffic observations by leveraging spatial and temporal dependencies across the road network. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approaches primarily rely on neighborhood aggregation to capture spatial dependencies, thereby modeling traffic interactions implicitly and making it difficult to accurately recover traffic magnitudes at locations without historical observations. To address this limitation, we propose LINK, a Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-node propagation rule learning paradigm for traffic Kriging. translated_title: LINK：面向交通克里金的轻量级归纳式节点间传播规则学习
translated_abstract: 时空交通克里金旨在利用路网中的空间和时间依赖性，在没有历史交通观测数据的未观测位置重建交通时间序列。现有的基于图神经网络（GNN）的方法主要依赖邻域聚合来捕捉空间依赖性，从而隐式地建模交通交互，这使得难以在没有历史观测数据的位置准确恢复交通量数值。为解决这一局限，我们提出了LINK——一种用于交通克里金的轻量级归纳式节点间传播规则学习范式。LINK引入了三个关键设计：1）以传播为中心的交通克里金范式，显式学习共享的节点间转移规则；2）上下文感知的谱传播网络，可在谱域和时域执行交通状态传播；3）TraffiKrig，一个真实的交通（数据/基准，原文截断）
tldr: LINK提出一种以传播为中心的轻量级归纳学习范式，通过显式学习共享的节点间传播规则并在谱域与时域进行交通状态传播，显著提升了无历史观测位置交通克里金重建的准确性。
en_tdlr: LINK proposes a lightweight, propagation-centric inductive learning paradigm that explicitly learns a shared node-to-node propagation rule and performs traffic-state propagation in both spectral and time domains, improving the accuracy of traffic kriging at locations without historical observations.
